THE SEED IDEA (from a Telegram brainstorm between the user, Alexander Didenko, and a friend — original Russian, translated):

- "Морской бой, в котором ты имеешь право переставлять корабли как угодно, если данные, которые ты сообщил при выстрелах врага остаются верными (попал, убил, мимо). И ты можешь это делать перед каждым выстрелом врага."
  => Battleship where the DEFENDER may rearrange their fleet arbitrarily between enemy shots, as long as every answer already given (hit / kill / miss) remains true of the new arrangement. Allowed before every enemy shot.
- "Понятно, что машина это легко сделает. Но вот человеку такая комбинаторика может быть сложна."
  => A machine can do this combinatorics trivially; a human cannot. (=> the game must do the combinatorics FOR the human player, and make it legible.)
- "это тоже будет восьмибитная игра" => it must be an 8-bit game.
- "тут идея в множественности реальностей" => the theme is multiplicity of realities.
- "у тебя есть двигатель Алькубьерре. Он не позволяет уйти ни в будущее ни в прошлое, но он позволяет по бране перейти в соседнюю версию реальности где космические корабли по другому стояли."
  => An Alcubierre drive: no time travel, but you can cross the BRANE into a neighbouring version of reality where the ships stood differently. (This is the in-fiction justification for rearranging.)
- "Лавкрафтовскую историю надо брать. Непознанный темный бог искажает реальность там, где ты ее не пришпилил."
  => Lovecraftian framing: an unknowable dark god twists reality wherever you have NOT pinned it down. (This is the perfect fictional statement of the core mechanic: unobserved = unfixed = hostile.)
- "Либо это битва с доктором Стрэнжем, который смотрит 14млн вариантов сценариев и выбирает нужный" (+ a Doctor Strange gif)
  => The 14,000,605 futures reference. Suggests a visible COUNTER of remaining consistent realities.
- "Смотри, каждая твоя перестановка открывает дорогу в мультивселенную" / "Но каждый мой выстрел накрывает корабли сразу во всех ветках!"
  => Every rearrangement opens a road into the multiverse; a shot lands in ALL branches at once.
- "есть особый снаряд которым я могу накрыть сразу несколько альтернативных веток"
  => a special munition that covers several alternative branches at once.
- Warhammer 40k GELLER FIELD was raised: "Генераторы поля создают вокруг корабля почти невидимую энергетическую завесу — своеобразный пузырь реальности. Внутри этого пузыря продолжают действовать законы физического пространства-времени, а не хаотичные и извращённые правила Имматериума."
  => A bubble of STABLE reality. Obvious mechanic: project it onto a region and reality inside is PINNED — cannot shift any more. Literally "пришпилить реальность".
- Working title floated by the friend: "Рыцари и лжецы в мультивселенной безумия" (Knights and Liars in the Multiverse of Madness).
- The user's verdict on the state of the idea: "короче надо докрутить" (needs finishing/tightening).

WHAT THE USER ASKED FOR NOW (verbatim):
"Мне нужна новая 8битная игра. Я вообще без понятия как ты ее сделаешь и в каком лоре. Но она должна быть такая же крутая как десант Nostromo."
=> A new 8-bit game, lore is my call, it must be as cool as the Nostromo landing game (the existing project 'nostromo-gambit'). The user then said: work maximally autonomously, they are going to sleep. So: NO questions can be asked. Make confident decisions and justify them.

MY WORKING DIRECTION (challenge it if it is wrong, but this is the frame):
The player is the ATTACKER hunting a fleet that exists in superposition. The enemy fleet is not "hidden" — it is genuinely UNDETERMINED, collapsing only where the player has pinned it. The HUD's centrepiece is a big counter of remaining consistent realities, ticking down from millions. The visual signature is GHOST FLEETS: faint flickering silhouettes of sampled possible placements drawn over the enemy grid, converging into solid hulls as the possibility space collapses. Symmetrically, the PLAYER's own fleet also evades — the machine does that combinatorics for the human — but evading costs a resource and feeds the dark god.

CONSTRAINT: the deliverable must be a finished, polished, self-contained 8-bit game of the same production quality and scale as the existing 'nostromo-gambit' project. Not a prototype, not a toy. It must be genuinely fun to a human, not just conceptually clever.



=== REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (nostromo-gambit — the quality bar) ===
Path: G:\Другие компьютеры\PAULEKMAN\dev\nostromo-gambit  — this is a MIRROR (source-only, no node_modules). The LIVE, runnable working copy is C:\dev\nostromo-gambit. They are byte-identical except (a) C: has one extra file scripts\mutation-check.mjs, (b) C:\dev\...\public\app.js is 3 lines newer (a banner-phase reset). Sync direction is C: -> G: via `npm run mirror` (scripts/mirror-to-drive.mjs). NEVER run npm install on G:.
Stack: NO BUILD TOOLING AT ALL. No bundler, no transpiler, no framework, no CSS preprocessor, no TypeScript, no test framework package.

- Runtime: Node >= 22, `"type": "module"`, plain ESM `.mjs` everywhere on the server.
- Exactly ONE npm dependency in the whole project: `"chess.js": "1.4.0"`. Zero devDependencies. Tests run on the built-in `node --test`.
- Server: raw `node:http` + a hand-written 9-route router (src/server/http.mjs), a hand-written static file server (src/server/static.mjs) and a hand-written SSE hub (src/server/sse.mjs). Comment at the top of http.mjs: "Маршрутизатор на node:http. Никаких фреймворков — маршрутов девять."
- Client: three plain ES modules loaded with `<script type="module" src="/app.js">`, no imports from any CDN, no npm packages on the front end. `public/app.js` uses top-level `await` (it is a module).
- Rendering: NOT canvas. NOT React. Plain DOM + CSS transforms + inline SVG generated in JS. Board = 64 permanent `<div class="sq">` in a CSS grid + a separate absolutely-positioned `.pieces` layer where each piece is a `<div class="piece">` moved by `transform: translate(%,%)`.
- Transport: one GET /api/state + one SSE stream GET /api/events + five POST endpoints. No WebSocket.
- External engine: official Stockfish binary, downloaded at setup time into %LOCALAPPDATA%, driven as a SEPARATE PROCESS over UCI (deliberate weak coupling for GPL reasons). Not bundled, not in the repo.
- Zero external assets: no image files, no font files, no audio files, no icon files. The favicon is an inline `data:image/svg+xml` in index.html.
- package.json scripts: setup / start / test / test:unit / test:real / selfplay / audit / e2e / mirror / bench.
- .npmrc pins the npm cache to C: (`cache=C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\npm-cache`, `fund=false`, `audit=false`).
Scale: ~6149 lines of game code.
Files: Runtime game code = 6,149 lines (src 4,215 + public 1,934). Shipped total including tests and tooling = 8,857 lines of code + 350 lines of Russian docs.

public/ — 1,934 lines, THE PART THE NEW GAME MOST NEEDS TO MATCH
  theme.css        571 lines / 18.3 KB  — the entire 8-bit CRT look
  app.js           547 lines / 22.2 KB  — event stream, rendering, input, start screen
  sprites.js       410 lines / 11.4 KB  — 16x16 ASCII bitmaps -> SVG
  board.js         226 lines /  9.4 KB  — 64 squares, piece diffing, pointer input
  index.html       180 lines /  8.7 KB  — full static skeleton, every panel pre-declared

src/ — 4,215 lines
  game/dropGenerator.mjs 474  game/fen.mjs 282  game/dropRules.mjs 251
  game/marginal.mjs 222  game/game.mjs 356  game/packages.mjs 166
  game/sharpness.mjs 121  game/storytellers.mjs 107  game/computer.mjs 76
  game/rng.mjs 76  game/dice.mjs 51  game/fischer.mjs 60
  engine/uci.mjs 407  engine/pool.mjs 277  engine/evaluate.mjs 166
  engine/registry.mjs 145  engine/mock.mjs 141  engine/analysis.mjs 123
  server/main.mjs 360  server/http.mjs 115  server/sse.mjs 114  server/static.mjs 56
  shared/paths.mjs 69

scripts/ — 1,053 lines
  get-stockfish.mjs 471, selfplay.mjs 305, bench-drops.mjs 139, corpus.mjs 66,
  mirror-to-drive.mjs 60, stockfish.lock.json 12  (+ mutation-check.mjs on C: only)

test/ — 1,655 lines, 118 tests, all green in ~14 s
  unit/*.test.mjs (7 files, 101 tests) run against an in-process MockEngine so they
  finish in seconds; integration/http.test.mjs (229 lines, 17 tests) boots the REAL
  server on port 0 and parses raw SSE frames; helpers/server.mjs 112;
  fixtures/fake-engine.mjs 156; e2e/serve-for-e2e.mjs 35.

Docs: README.md 169 lines, REPORT.md 181 lines — both in Russian, both written as prose
for the user (not for a machine), both include a "known limitations / what was NOT done"
section. Matching that documentation standard is part of the quality bar.
Aesthetic: "Ship's terminal": green phosphor vs amber phosphor on near-black, scanlines, vignette, brightness flicker. Every pixel is CSS or generated SVG — comment at the top of theme.css: "Всё рисуется CSS — ни одной картинки, ни одного внешнего шрифта."

PALETTE (public/theme.css :root, exact hex):
  --phosphor:       #7dff9b   green phosphor = side 1 (marines / white)
  --phosphor-dim:   #3d8a52   secondary text, borders on buttons
  --phosphor-faint: #1c3d27   tertiary text, coordinates, "nothing here yet"
  --amber:          #ffb347   amber phosphor = side 2 (xenos / black), all warnings
  --amber-dim:      #8a5f26
  --alert:          #ff4d4d   only for the broken-link dot
  --bg:             #050a06   page ground
  --panel:          #0a140c   panel fill
  --panel-edge:     #16301c   every 1px border, every separator
  --light-square:   #17301d
  --dark-square:    #0d1e11
Literal one-off colors: check square background #3a0f0f; eval-bar label text #dfffe8 on
rgba(5,10,6,0.78); overlay scrim rgba(5,10,6,0.9); glow shadows are
rgba(125,255,155,0.x) for green and rgba(255,179,71,0.x) for amber.

SPRITE PALETTE (public/sprites.js, per side, 4 colors each):
  w: { x:'#06170c'  outline, '#':'#7dff9b' body, o:'#dcffe6' highlight, '*':'#ffd166' accent }
  b: { x:'#1d0f00'  outline, '#':'#ffb347' body, o:'#ffe3ba' highlight, '*':'#b6ff5a' accent }
Doctrine stated in the file: the two sides differ by HUE, not by brightness, so they stay
legible on a dim CRT — and both hues are real period monitor phosphors.

FONT: `--font: 'Consolas', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', 'Courier New', monospace;` — system mono
only, no webfont, no @font-face, nothing loaded from Google Fonts. Body 14px,
`letter-spacing: 0.04em`. Titles are wide-tracked uppercase: `.title` 17px/0.22em,
`.start-title` 25px/0.3em, panel `<h2>` 11px/0.2em, buttons 12px/0.12em.
Text-shadow glow on titles only: `0 0 8px rgba(125,255,155,0.5)` / `0 0 14px …0.45`.

SPRITE TECHNIQUE (this is the signature move, copy it verbatim):
16 rows x 16 chars of ASCII, one string per row, 4 symbols: `.` transparent, `x` outline,
`#` body, `o` highlight, `*` accent. `spriteSvg()` walks each row, run-length-merges
horizontally identical pixels into one `<rect>`, and emits
`<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" shape-rendering="crispEdges" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">`.
Results are memoized in a `Map` keyed `set:color:type`. The RLE is not decoration — the
comment says without it the board would cost >4000 DOM nodes in pieces alone.
Two full sets exist: `classic` (traditional silhouettes) and `xeno` (marines vs xenomorphs),
switchable at runtime from the settings drawer.

RESOLUTION / SCALING: there is no fixed canvas. Board is `--board-max: min(72vh, 560px)`
(mobile: `min(92vw, 520px)`), squares are a `repeat(8,1fr)` grid, each piece is
`width:12.5%; height:12.5%` with `.piece svg { padding: 7%; image-rendering: pixelated }`.
So a 16x16 bitmap renders at ~65px and stays crisp via crispEdges + pixelated.

CRT EFFECT — one pseudo-element over everything, click-through:
  body::after { position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none; z-index:100;
    background:
      repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(0,0,0,.22) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px),
      radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 55%, rgba(0,0,0,.55) 100%);
    animation: flicker 5.5s infinite steps(60); }
`steps(60)` is what makes the flicker read as a CRT and not as a fade. The flicker
keyframes only dip at 97%/99% (0.93 / 0.96) — subtle, never distracting.

MOTION VOCABULARY (exact durations — reuse these numbers, they are tuned):
  piece move          transform 180ms ease-out (piece never re-created, only translated)
  drop landing        340ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), starts 44px above with
                      scale(1.7) and opacity 0 — overshoot reads as a LANDING
  shockwave ring      460ms ease-out, scale(0.2)->2.2, opacity .7->0, amber border
  banner slide        translateY(-100%) -> 0, 220ms ease-out
  drawer slide        translateX(100%) -> 0, 200ms ease-out
  eval bar            height/width 260ms ease-out
  toast               opacity+translateY 200ms, auto-hides after 3400ms
  die shake           90ms infinite ±1px/±4deg; spin redraws every 70ms for 700ms
  boot typewriter     9ms per character, 120ms per line break
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` appears THREE times and kills the flicker, the
piece transition, the landing animation and the shockwave. Non-negotiable for parity.

LAYOUT: one CSS grid with named areas —
  grid-template-areas: 'head head head' / 'evalbar board side' / 'foot foot foot'
  grid-template-columns: 42px var(--board-max) minmax(300px, 1fr)
  max-width 1240px, `overflow:hidden` on html/body (desktop), gap 12px, padding 10px 14px.
At `max-width: 980px` it collapses to a single column, areas reorder to
'head' 'evalbar' 'board' 'foot' 'side', and the vertical eval bar becomes a horizontal
22px strip whose gradient direction flips. Note the file ends with a DUPLICATED narrow
media block and an explicit comment explaining that a later `.foot { flex-wrap: nowrap }`
rule won on equal specificity, so the mobile rules had to be repeated last. That kind of
comment — the fix plus why — is the house style.

CHROME DETAILS worth copying: 1px `--panel-edge` borders on everything; panel headers are
11px 0.2em uppercase dim-green on a bordered strip; buttons are transparent with a dim
border and hover = 10% tint + 8px glow; segmented controls (`.seg`) collapse borders with
`border-right-width:0` except `:last-child`, and the active one gets
`inset 0 0 10px rgba(125,255,155,.18)`; dice are 3x3 CSS grids of 5px round `<i>` pips;
`.pips` uses `●●●○○` text characters for remaining rolls; separators in the move log are
`border-top: 1px dashed var(--amber-dim)` with the text `═══ ДЕСАНТ #3 ═══`.
Audio: THERE IS NO AUDIO. NONE. I grepped the entire project (both the G: mirror and the C: live copy) for AudioContext / createOscillator / webkitAudioContext / `new Audio(` / sound / звук / audio — zero matches. There is no audio engine, no chiptune player, no sound file, no mute toggle, no volume setting, no `<audio>` element, no gesture-unlock code.

This is the single biggest gap in the reference project and the clearest place where the second game can EXCEED the bar rather than merely match it. Do not go looking for a helper to copy — there is nothing. If the new game wants sound, it must be written from scratch.

Constraints the new audio code must respect to stay consistent with the project's doctrine:
1. Zero external assets and zero dependencies. That rules out sample files and audio libraries; it means WebAudio synthesis (oscillators + gain envelopes + a noise buffer) written by hand, the same way sprites are hand-generated rather than shipped as PNGs.
2. Autoplay policy: nostromo-gambit has an explicit first-click gate already available — the `#start-go` "▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ" button on the start screen is guaranteed to be a user gesture. That is where `new AudioContext()` should be created / resumed.
3. It must honour the same accessibility instinct as `prefers-reduced-motion`: an audio on/off checkbox belongs in the settings drawer next to "Показывать шкалу оценки", persisted through the same settings POST, and it must default in a way that never surprises.
4. Every sound needs a named, motivated trigger the same way every animation does — the existing event vocabulary gives the hook points for free: `move`, `drop:start`, `drop:progress`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`, `dice`, `thinking`, check, game over, boot typewriter keyclick.
5. Palette discipline translates to audio: two timbres for the two sides (green/amber), one alert timbre, nothing else — the same "two hues, not two brightnesses" logic.
Architecture: SHAPE: a local single-player-at-one-screen web app with an authoritative Node server. The client is deliberately stupid. Top of public/app.js, verbatim:

  // Клиент намеренно ничего не решает сам: легальность ходов, расписание десанта
  // и счёт жетонов живут на сервере и приходят готовыми. Здесь только три вещи —
  // отрисовка, ввод указателя и тайминги анимаций.

THERE IS NO GAME LOOP. No requestAnimationFrame, no setInterval tick, no fixed timestep,
no update()/draw() split anywhere in the project. The app is 100% event-driven: server
state changes -> SSE frame -> `applyState(next)` -> full re-render of a small DOM. All
motion is delegated to CSS transitions/animations. The only timers in the client are the
dice spin (`setInterval(…, 70)` for 700 ms), the boot typewriter (chained `setTimeout`),
the toast dismissal (3400 ms) and shockwave cleanup (500 ms). If the second game needs a
real-time loop, that pattern must be invented — there is nothing here to copy.

SERVER STATE MACHINE — `class Game` (src/game/game.mjs), 356 lines:
  phase: 'idle' | 'dropping' | 'over'   (set in #refreshGameOver)
  version: monotonically incremented on EVERY mutation; it is both the SSE event id and
           the optimistic-concurrency token.
  Own journal instead of the library's: `atoms[]` (each `{kind:'move'|'drop', …}`) plus a
  parallel `snapshots[]` stack of FENs. Reason is documented at the top of the file —
  chess.js 1.4.0 `load()` calls `clear()` and destroys its own history, and the drop
  mechanic must rebuild the position from FEN, so undo/move-list/threefold would have
  silently vanished. There is a regression test for exactly this.
  Stable piece identity: `this.pieces` is a Map square -> `{id:'p17', type, color}`.
  IDs are assigned from a module-level `nextPieceId` counter and are what makes the client
  animate instead of blink. `#applyPieceMove(m)` transfers the id using the SEMANTICS of
  the move (en-passant victim square, castling rook hop, promotion type swap) because you
  cannot infer identity by diffing two positions.
  Honest degradation: after undo, ids are re-issued (`#rebuildPieceIds`) and the board
  redraws wholesale, with a comment saying this is more honest than pretending.

APP ORCHESTRATOR — `class App` (src/server/main.mjs), 360 lines: owns sessionId (randomUUID),
Game, SseHub, EnginePool, AnalysisEngine, Rng, and the `dropInProgress` / `dropAbort` pair.
Async work (computer move, drop search) is deliberately NOT awaited inside the HTTP handler:

  // Намеренно не await: ход считается в фоне, а состояние уезжает клиенту событием.
  // Иначе HTTP-ответ на ход человека ждал бы, пока движок додумает свой…

and every background task re-checks `this.game.version !== versionAtStart` before applying
its result, because the game may have been reset/undone while it was thinking.

SCREENS (there are no routes; screens are stacked z-indexed overlays in one HTML file):
  .start   z-index 90  full-screen start card, `.off` hides it
  .drawer  z-index 60  settings, slides in from the right
  .overlay z-index 50  two of them: game-over card and promotion picker; `.on` shows
  .toast   z-index 70  transient message
  body::after z-index 100 CRT layer above everything, pointer-events none
The start screen is shown ONLY when there is nothing to resume — last 8 lines of app.js:
`const gameInProgress = state && (state.moveLog.length > 0 || state.dropLog.length > 0)`;
if resuming it shows the toast «ПАРТИЯ ВОССТАНОВЛЕНА» instead. This exists because a
reload mid-game used to cover a live board with a screen whose only button would erase it.

HTTP API (src/server/http.mjs): GET /api/state, GET /api/events, GET /health,
POST /api/move | /api/roll | /api/new-game | /api/undo | /api/settings,
POST /api/_test/fen (only when NODE_ENV=test). One `STATUS` table maps error codes to
HTTP statuses (409 for conflicts, 422 for illegal move, 503 for engine down). Body limit
64 KB. Errors are caught so a bad request never kills a game in progress.

OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: client sends `version: state.version` with move/roll/undo; a
mismatch returns `{code:'STALE_VERSION'}` and the client treats it as non-error and just
re-reads state (`if (data.code === 'STALE_VERSION') { await refresh(); return data; }`).

EVENT STREAM: exactly ONE multiplexed SSE endpoint, with the reason spelled out — HTTP/1.1
allows ~6 connections per origin, two streams x two tabs already eats four. Event names:
`snapshot`, `state`, `move`, `settings` (all carry a full snapshot and an `id:`),
plus volatile `eval`, `thinking`, `drop:progress` (NO `id:`, so they cannot poison
Last-Event-ID), plus `dice`, `drop:start`, `drop:done`, `drop:skipped`.
A 200-frame ring buffer replays from Last-Event-ID; if there is a gap it falls back to a
full snapshot. 15 s heartbeat comments, `retry: 3000`, `setNoDelay(true)` (Nagle was
batching 60-byte eval frames into 40 ms jerks), `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `no-transform`.

INPUT (public/board.js `#bindPointer`): Pointer Events only — NOT HTML5 drag&drop, with
the reason in a comment (ghost image, no touch support, no control over animation). Two
interaction modes on the same handler: drag (pointerdown -> capture -> pointermove sets
`transform` in px -> pointerup hit-tests) and click-click (select source, then click a
highlighted target). `#squareFromPoint(x,y)` converts client coords via
`getBoundingClientRect()` and a /8 floor. On release the piece is ALWAYS snapped back
locally and the server's echo is what actually moves it. `board.setLocked()` freezes input
during a drop and after game over. `.board { touch-action: none; user-select: none }`.
Keyboard: only `Escape` (closes drawer + promo, clears selection).

PERSISTENCE: there is none on the client — no localStorage, no cookies, no save file.
State lives in server memory; a page reload re-fetches it. Runtime artifacts (engine
binary, selfplay NDJSON, PID registry) live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nostromo-gambit\` via
src/shared/paths.mjs, deliberately NOT next to the sources, because the source folder is
on a Google Drive virtual volume. `writeJsonAtomic()` = write .tmp then rename.

DETERMINISM: `makeRng(seed)` (xorshift128+) everywhere; `Math.random` appears exactly once
in the whole client and only to spin the dice faces visually. Same seed reproduces the
whole game including the Fischer start position (`fischerFen(makeRng('fischer:'+seed))`).
Reusable helpers: Verbatim signatures of the helpers worth lifting into the second game.

PIXEL-ART RENDERER (public/sprites.js) — the highest-value single function:
  export const PALETTES = { w: {...}, b: {...} }          // 4 keys: x # o *
  export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) -> string   // memoized, RLE'd SVG
  export const PIECE_LETTER = { p:'П', n:'К', b:'С', r:'Л', q:'Ф', k:'Кр' }
  export const PIECE_NAME   = { p:'пешка', ... }
Generalize by renaming `setName/color/type` to `(setName, paletteKey, spriteKey)` and
keeping the ASCII-bitmap-as-string-array authoring format unchanged.

BOARD / SPRITE LAYER (public/board.js) — a reusable "grid of cells + diffed sprite layer":
  export function squareName(file, rank)
  export class BoardView {
    constructor({ squaresEl, piecesEl, boardEl, onSelect })
    render(board, { legalMoves = {}, lastMove = null, checkSquare = null,
                    reinforced = [], landedIds = null } = {})
    select(sq); clearSelection();
    shockwave(squares);                  // spawns .shock spans, self-removing after 500ms
    setLocked(locked); setPieceSet(name, badges);
    #buildSquares(); #bindPointer(); #squareFromPoint(x, y); #placePiece(el, square);
    #createPiece(p);
  }
The load-bearing idea to copy: cells are built ONCE and never re-created; entities live in
a sibling absolutely-positioned layer, are keyed by a server-assigned stable id, and are
moved with `--tx/--ty` custom properties + `transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty))`.
That one decision is what turns "re-render" into "animation".

TOAST (public/app.js) — 6 lines, uses a property on the function itself as the timer slot:
  function toast(text) { el.toast.textContent = text; el.toast.classList.add('on');
    clearTimeout(toast.t); toast.t = setTimeout(() => el.toast.classList.remove('on'), 3400); }

TYPEWRITER BOOT SEQUENCE (public/app.js):

HONESTY AS A DESIGN PRINCIPLE. This is the strongest through-line and the thing that makes
the project feel expensive. When something cannot be done properly it is disabled and said
out loud, in the UI, not hidden: Fischer castling is off and the start screen says so;
a failed drop refunds the die and prints the reason; a widened tolerance is written into
the drop log as «ДОПУСК РАСШИРЕН ДО ±45 СП»; undo after a drop admits it must redraw the
whole board. README and REPORT both end with «Известные ограничения» / «Что осталось
несделанным». The second game must have that section too.

OPENING. Not a splash screen — a configuration terminal, exactly like an era game. The
boot text types itself character by character (9 ms/char, 120 ms/line) above the title,
then a single card asks EVERYTHING at once via segmented buttons: player 1 human/computer,
player 2 human/computer, computer level 1–5, planner, start position, dice rolls per
player, auto-drop frequency. Every option has a live one-line explanatory note under it
(`.opt-note`, amber-dim) that changes as you select — the level note, the planner blurb,
the Fischer caveat. One amber call-to-action: «▶ НАЧАТЬ ОПЕРАЦИЮ». Under it, one honest
line about the 32-piece ceiling.

DIFFICULTY. Five named levels with character, not numbers: 1 РЯДОВОЙ / 2 КАПРАЛ /
3 СЕРЖАНТ / 4 ЛЕЙТЕНАНТ / 5 MU-TH-UR 6000 («Полная сила на этой машине. Удачи.»).
Default is 3. Crucially, weakening is done by MultiPV move selection within a `slackCp`
window (220/130/60/20/0), NOT by cutting depth — with the stated reason: a depth-starved
engine plays *stranger*, not weaker; it still never blunders two-move tactics but stops
having a plan. Even level 1 is forbidden from gifting a queen.

PACING. Turn-based, no timers, no pressure. The drama is manufactured in two places:
(1) the drop — a banner slides down over the board, the board dims to 0.55 and goes
`cursor:wait`, a phase-weighted progress bar advances through four named phases
(weights 0.05/0.2/0.55/1.0 so the bar never lies about which stage it is in), and it ends
with pieces falling from above with an overshoot plus amber shockwave rings and a toast;
(2) the dice — 700 ms of shaking, faces reshuffling every 70 ms, then the readout line
that tells you exactly what you bought. Search takes 4–6 s in practice and REPORT.md says
plainly that this was over the 2.5 s target — the progress bar with meaningful phase names
is the accepted mitigation: "ожидание читается как работа, а не как зависание."

WHAT MAKES IT FEEL GOOD. (a) Nothing ever blinks: stable piece ids mean every change is a
motion. (b) Every number shown is explained somewhere — the drop log prints
`+0.34 → +0.29 · Δ -5 сп · ЦЕЛЬ 0 · 4.2 с` and the header prints the hold count.
(c) Personality lives in tables, not in code branches — three "planners" (МАТЬ / БИШОП /
ЭШ, borrowed conceptually from RimWorld storytellers) differ only by weights and tolerance,
each with a `tone: { start, done, skipped }` string triple; ЭШ's line is
«ВЫСАДКА ВЫПОЛНЕНА. НЕ МОГУ ЛГАТЬ О ВАШИХ ШАНСАХ.». (d) Tension is built into the dice
math rather than into UI noise: sum buys tonnage, spread buys bias, and a double gives max
tonnage with ZERO bias while 6–1 gives max bias with almost no tonnage — you cannot have
both. (e) The one aesthetic ruling the user made mid-build is recorded in REPORT.md and
worth internalizing: the eval bar used to be "green vs empty", which speaks the language of
white and black; it was recolored to green-vs-amber so it speaks the language of THIS
game's two sides.

ENDING. A centered card over a 0.9 scrim: the reason in huge tracked caps («МАТ»), one
statistics line («Ходов: 47 · Десантов: 6 · Фигур на доске: 21»), and two buttons —
«НОВАЯ ПАРТИЯ» (returns to the configuration terminal, never straight into a game) and
«ПОСМОТРЕТЬ ПАРТИЮ» (dismisses the card so you can study the final position). There is also
`Game.toPgn()` which exports the game with drops as PGN comments, so a game can be re-read.

//   .  прозрачно      x  контур       #  тело
//   o  блик           *  акцент (визор морпеха, кислота ксеноморфа)

export const PALETTES = {
  w: { x: '#06170c', '#': '#7dff9b', o: '#dcffe6', '*': '#ffd166' },
  b: { x: '#1d0f00', '#': '#ffb347', o: '#ffe3ba', '*': '#b6ff5a' },
};

const cache = new Map();

/**
 * Разворачивает битмап в SVG. Соседние пиксели одного цвета склеиваются в один
 * прямоугольник по горизонтали: без этого на доску уходило бы больше четырёх тысяч
 * узлов DOM только под фигуры.
 */
export function spriteSvg(setName, color, type) {
  const key = `${setName}:${color}:${type}`;
  if (cache.has(key)) return cache.get(key);

  const set = SETS[setName] || SETS.xeno;
  const rows = (set[color] || set.w)[type] || CLASSIC[type];
  const palette = PALETTES[color];
  const parts = [];

  for (let y = 0; y < rows.length; y++) {
    const row = rows[y];
    let x = 0;
    while (x < row.length) {
      const ch = row[x];
      if (ch === '.' || ch === ' ') { x += 1; continue; }
      let run = 1;
      while (x + run < row.length && row[x + run] === ch) run += 1;
      const fill = palette[ch] || palette['#'];
      parts.push(`<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${run}" height="1" fill="${fill}"/>`);
      x += run;
    }

  /**
   * Указатель, а не нативный drag&drop: последний тащит призрачную картинку,
   * не работает на касании и не даёт управлять анимацией. Плюс поддержан
   * режим «клик по источнику — клик по цели», которым играет большинство.
   */
  #bindPointer() {
    let dragging = null;

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', (ev) => {
      if (this.locked) return;
      const sq = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!sq) return;

      // Второй клик по подсвеченной цели завершает ход.
      if (this.selected && this.legalMoves[this.selected]?.includes(sq)) {
        this.onSelect({ from: this.selected, to: sq });
        this.clearSelection();
        return;
      }

      const piece = this.board.find((p) => p.square === sq);
      if (!piece || !this.legalMoves[sq]) { this.clearSelection(); return; }

      this.select(sq);
      const el = this.pieceEls.get(piece.id);
      if (!el) return;
      dragging = { from: sq, el, pointerId: ev.pointerId, moved: false };
      el.classList.add('dragging');
      this.boardEl.setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId);
      ev.preventDefault();
    });

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointermove', (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
      const size = rect.width / 8;
      const x = ev.clientX - rect.left - size / 2;
      const y = ev.clientY - rect.top - size / 2;
      dragging.moved = true;
      dragging.el.style.transform = `translate(${x}px, ${y}px)`;
    });

    const finish = (ev) => {
      if (!dragging) return;
      const { from, el, moved } = dragging;
      dragging = null;
      el.classList.remove('dragging');
      el.style.transform = '';
      this.#placePiece(el, from); // вернём на место; сервер подтвердит настоящий ход
      try { this.boardEl.releasePointerCapture(ev.pointerId); } catch { /* захват мог уже отпуститься сам */ }
      if (!moved) return; // это был обычный клик — выбор уже сделан
      const to = this.#squareFromPoint(ev.clientX, ev.clientY);
      if (!to || to === from) return;
      if (!this.legalMoves[from]?.includes(to)) return;
      this.onSelect({ from, to });
      this.clearSelection();
    };

    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointerup', finish);
    this.boardEl.addEventListener('pointercancel', finish);
  }

  #squareFromPoint(x, y) {
    const rect = this.boardEl.getBoundingClientRect();
    const f = Math.floor(((x - rect.left) / rect.width) * 8);
    const r = 8 - Math.floor(((y - rect.top) / rect.height) * 8);
    if (f < 0 || f > 7 || r < 1 || r > 8) return null;
    return squareName(f, r);
  }

export class Rng {
  constructor(seed = 'nostromo') {
    this.seed = String(seed);
    const [a, b, c, d] = hashSeed(seed);
    this.s = new Uint32Array([a, b, c, d]);
    // Прокручиваем, чтобы близкие сиды не давали похожих первых чисел.
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) this.next();
  }
  next() {                                   // xorshift128+, uint32
    let t = this.s[3]; const s0 = this.s[0];
    this.s[3] = this.s[2]; this.s[2] = this.s[1]; this.s[1] = s0;
    t ^= t << 11; t ^= t >>> 8;
    this.s[0] = (t ^ s0 ^ (s0 >>> 19)) >>> 0;
    return this.s[0];
  }
  float() { return this.next() / 4294967296; }
  int(min, max) { if (max < min) return min; return min + (this.next() % (max - min + 1)); }
  pick(arr) { if (!arr || arr.length === 0) return undefined; return arr[this.next() % arr.length]; }
  shuffle(arr) { for (let i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--) { const j = this.next() % (i + 1); [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]]; } return arr; }
  weighted(items, weightOf = (x) => x.weight) {
    const total = items.reduce((s, x) => s + Math.max(0, weightOf(x)), 0);
    if (total <= 0) return this.pick(items);
    let roll = this.float() * total;
    for (const item of items) { roll -= Math.max(0, weightOf(item)); if (roll <= 0) return item; }
    return items[items.length - 1];
  }
  /** Отдельный поток случайности, привязанный к метке — чтобы ветки не сдвигали друг друга. */
  fork(label) { return new Rng(`${this.seed}:${label}:${this.next()}`); }
}
export function makeRng(seed) { return new Rng(seed); }

content.text: # JUICE DIRECTION — «ПРОТОКОЛ ГЕЛЛЕРА» *(alt title: «14 000 605». Subtitle: МОРСКОЙ БОЙ В МУЛЬТИВСЕЛЕННОЙ · ТАКТИЧЕСКИЙ МОДУЛЬ)* ## 0. The one architectural break from the reference, and why nostromo-gambit has **no rAF loop and no canvas** — every motion is a CSS transition on a stable-id DOM node. That works because chess has ≤32 entities that move once per second. Here the enemy grid must draw ~8 overlapping translucent fleet silhouettes *plus* a 100-cell dithered probability field, reshuffling continuously. That is 500+ draw ops per frame. DOM cannot do it, and CSS cannot express additive blending. **Decision: hybrid.** Chrome (header, HUD panels, counter, logs, drawer, overlays, toast, CRT layer) stays DOM + `theme.css`, lifted verbatim. Only the two grids become ``, with one shared `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Comment to write at the top of `render.mjs`: ```js // Единственный rAF во всём проекте. В «Ностромо» цикла не было и не требовалось: // там тридцать две сущности двигались раз в секунду и CSS справлялся сам. // Здесь на вражеской сетке кипит восемь наложенных силуэтов и поле вероятностей // из ста ячеек — это пятьсот операций рисования на кадр. DOM столько не тянет, // а сложение прозрачностей ('lighter') в CSS не выражается вовсе. ``` **Canvas resolution: 160×160 internal per board** (10×10 cells × 16 px — the same 16 px module as the reference sprites). Scaled by an **integer** factor only: `scale = Math.max(1, Math.floor(cssPx / 160))`, `ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, `image-rendering: pixelated`. At 480 px CSS that is ×3. Never a fractional scale — half-pixels are how 8-bit dies. --- ## 1. GHOST FLEET — the draw algorithm Two layers, drawn bottom-up into the same canvas each frame. ### 1a. Probability field, as a 4×4 ordered dither (this is the signature move) The server sends a quantized occupancy field: `Uint8Array(100)`, value 0–16 = "in how many sixteenths of sampled realities is this cell occupied". Not an alpha ramp — **a count of lit sub-pixels**. Each 16×16 cell is subdivided into a 4×4 grid of 4×4-px blocks. A standard Bayer matrix decides which blocks are lit: ```js const BAYER4 = [ 0, 8, 2,10, 12, 4,14, 6, 3,11, 1, 9, 15, 7,13, 5]; // уровень L (0..16): блок i горит, если BAYER4[i] < L ``` Precompute **17 offscreen 16×16 tiles per hue** at load (`buildDitherTiles(hex)` → `OffscreenCanvas[17]`). Per frame the field costs exactly 100 `drawImage` calls. Zero per-pixel work. Why dither and not alpha: an alpha ramp at p=0.08 is a flat dim grey square and reads as *fog*. A 1-of-16 dither is a single lit 4×4 pixel in a black cell and reads as *a possibility*. It is also literally how an NES would have done it. ### 1b. Ghost silhouettes — additive, slot-staggered, held for 3 frames ```js const GHOST_SLOTS = 8; // сколько силуэтов живёт одновременно const SLOT_PERIOD = 24; // кадров жизни одного силуэта (400 мс) const SLOT_STAGGER = 7; // сдвиг фаз между слотами (24 и 7 взаимно просты) const GHOST_ALPHA = 0.075; // на один силуэт, режим 'lighter' ``` Each frame: `for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) if ((frame + i * SLOT_STAGGER) % SLOT_PERIOD === 0) slot[i] = pool.take();` — one replacement roughly every 3 frames, never all at once. The eye reads staggered 400 ms lifetimes as **boiling**; it reads a global 60 Hz reshuffle as **TV static**. This distinction is the entire difference between "delicious" and "unreadable". Then: ```js ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'; for (const g of slot) { ctx.globalAlpha = GHOST_ALPHA * g.fade; // fade: 0→1 за 4 кадра, 1→0 за 4 кадра ctx.fillStyle = WARP_RGB; for (const run of g.runs) ctx.fillRect(run.x*16 + g.jx, run.y*16 + g.jy, run.w*16, 16); } ctx.globalCompositeOperation = 'source-over'; ``` `g.runs` is the sample's occupancy bitmask **run-length-merged horizontally**, exactly the trick `sprites.js` uses to avoid 4000 DOM nodes: a 5-cell ship is one `fillRect`, not five. `g.jx/g.jy` is a ±1 px jitter chosen **once when the slot is filled**, not per frame — per-frame jitter is noise, per-ghost jitter is texture. **Convergence is free and needs no extra code.** Additive blending means a cell present in 1 of 8 ghosts sits at α 0.075 (barely there); a cell present in all 8 sits at α 0.6 and reads as a solid hull. As the possibility space collapses, samples agree, sums saturate, and the fleet *materialises out of its own agreement*. Nothing fades in. The ghosts simply start telling the same story. Write that in a comment. **Boil rate is a variable.** `SLOT_PERIOD` drops to 4 frames for 300 ms after any shot (`ВСКИПАНИЕ` — the possibility space visibly re-thinks), then eases back over 500 ms via `slotPeriod = 4 + 20 * ease(t)`. Reduced motion: `SLOT_SLOTS = 0`, draw the mean field only, statically. --- ## 2. THE REALITIES COUNTER Centre column, between the two boards, because it is physically between the two realities. `34px`, `letter-spacing: 0.18em`, 8 digit cells + thin-space group separators: `≈ 14 000 605`. **Honesty rule, borrowed from the reference's doctrine:** the exact count is #P-hard in general. The server counts exactly by DFS with pruning while the search stays under a `2e6`-node budget; above that it Monte-Carlo estimates. The estimate is prefixed `≈` and rendered in `--warp`. The moment the count becomes exact the tilde disappears and the digits shift to `--bone`. **The counter visibly stops lying at you.** That transition (usually around 10⁴) is one of the best beats in the game and it costs one CSS class. Odometer: each digit is a `0..9`, `overflow:hidden`, height 34px, the `` is a 10-glyph vertical strip translated by `translateY(-value * 34px)`, `transition: transform 260ms cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)` — the same overshoot curve as the landing animation, so the whole project speaks one motion language. Stagger `transition-delay: 18ms * (7 - index)` so the change ripples right-to-left. **COLLAPSE BEAT** — fires when `next < prev / 4`: 1. **Freeze frame, 90 ms.** The rAF loop early-returns; the last frame stays on screen. Music gain → 0.3 in 20 ms. 2. **Scramble, 400 ms.** Every digit that will change cycles random glyphs at 40 ms. 3. **Shake, 220 ms.** The `.app` gets `transform: translate(var(--sx), var(--sy))` driven by the loop: amplitude 5 px, three oscillations, decaying linearly, snapped to integer pixels. 4. Ghost layer drawn **twice** for 6 frames, at `(+1,0)` in `--warp` and `(-1,0)` in `--pinned` — an 8-bit chromatic split, not a shader. 5. Digits land. SFX: the 5-blip descending arpeggio (§7). Reduced motion: no freeze, no shake, no scramble; digits snap. --- ## 3. MISS / HIT / KILL — three escalating beats ### МИМО — a constraint, not nothing (the hardest one to get right) The point of the whole game is that a miss *destroys realities*. So make the destruction the animation, not the water splash. - The cell locks instantly to the **pinned-void tile**: `--void-hard #0a1418` fill, 1 px inset `--pinned-dim` border, a 2×2-px ✕ in `--pinned-dim` at the centre. Hard, cold, permanent. It never boils again. - **Culling, 180 ms.** Every ghost currently on screen that contained that cell is re-drawn in `--alert` at α 0.5 and **dissolves**: three steps at 60 ms, each dropping a random 35 % of its remaining 4×4 blocks (seeded from the deterministic `Rng` so replays match). You watch a hundred thousand futures come apart into red dust. - The counter drops. Ledger panel gets a line: `D4 · ПУСТО · −812 340 РЕАЛЬНОСТЕЙ`. **Every miss prints its own body count.** That number is the reward. A miss in this game should feel like a good move, and it will, because you can read exactly how much of the multiverse it cost the enemy. - SFX: dry bandpassed noise thud + a high 18 ms tick — the tick is the sound of *information being recorded*. ### ПОПАЛ - 2-frame full-board white flash: `--bone` at α 0.12 over everything, `'lighter'`. - The cell goes solid `--amber`. An expanding **square** ring: 1-cell outline growing one cell per 4 frames for 3 steps, each step dithered one level dimmer (16 → 10 → 5 → 0). Squares, not circles — the reference's round `.shock` belongs to CSS; on a 16 px pixel grid a square ring is more honest and reads better. - `ВСКИПАНИЕ`: boil rate to 4 frames for 300 ms while the sampler re-conditions. The possibility space visibly *lurches*. - Counter dive, usually a collapse beat. ### УБИТ — the full ceremony 1. 90 ms freeze frame. 2. The entire ship resolves at once: drawn from the real 16 px ship sprite set (RLE'd, same authoring format as `sprites.js`), full brightness, outline forced to `--bone` for 120 ms. 3. Screen shake 5 px / 3 oscillations / 220 ms. 4. **Hull burn, 700 ms**: hull pixels flip to `*` accent then to void, sweeping top-to-bottom one 4 px row per 40 ms. 5. Toast «КОРПУС РАЗРУШЕН · ЭСМИНЕЦ (3)». Ledger line. The largest counter dive of the game — killing a ship removes an entire degree of freedom, and the counter shows it. 6. Audio ducks to 0.35× for 600 ms. Escalation in one sentence, which is how it should be tuned: **miss = cold click + red dust; hit = white flash + boil; kill = freeze + shake + burn + the big number falling.** --- ## 4. PINNING REALITY — the Geller field Player action on **their own** board (which also boils — your fleet is undetermined too, and the machine does that combinatorics for you, per the seed idea). Spend one charge, select a 3×3 region: your ships inside it may never be moved by a future evasion again. Animation, 500 ms: - A **Bresenham circle** expands from the centre cell, 3 concentric 1-px rings, radius growing 16 px per 80 ms, drawn in `--pinned`. - As the ring passes over each cell, that cell's dither level is **quantised to 0 or 16**. Nothing in between. This is the whole idea made visible: *inside the field, probability has only two values.* - Per-cell jitter goes to 0 inside the bubble. The boil stops dead. Motion outside, stillness inside — the contrast is the payoff. - Hue switch violet → ice-cyan. - Border afterwards: 1 px dotted `--pinned` marching ants, offset cycling 0-1-2-3 at **8 fps** (four discrete steps, not a smooth CSS animation — 8-bit means quantised time too). - SFX: two sines rising 220→660 Hz whose mutual detune goes 40 cents → 0 over 420 ms, terminated by a hard 25 ms square click. The sound of two realities becoming one, then sealed. Charges shown as `●●○` pips in `--pinned`, reusing the existing `.pips` rule. --- ## 5. PERFORMANCE BUDGET (why 60 fps is not in doubt) Per board per frame: 100 `drawImage` (pre-baked dither tiles, 17 levels × 4 hues = 68 offscreen 16×16 canvases built once at load) + 8 ghosts × ≤17 RLE runs ≈ 136 `fillRect` + ~20 ops of chrome. ≈ 260 ops; two boards ≈ 520. On a 160×160 backing store that is well under 2 ms. The rules: **never compute dither per pixel; never allocate in the loop; never call `getImageData`; ghost samples arrive pre-RLE'd as `Uint8Array` bitmasks and are decoded once when a slot takes them.** Timing is in **frames**, not milliseconds, with a delta guard that skips logic if `dt > 100 ms` (tab was backgrounded). `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` kills, in order: the CRT flicker, the boil (static mean field only), the screen shake, the freeze frames, the odometer roll, the hull burn, and the marching ants. The game remains fully playable and fully legible — the dither field alone carries the information. --- ## 11.
